# A grid header toolbar measures items that are not built yet

## Context

Two sightings, both on Gantt examples while their columns were changed at runtime: Maryam's defect-note `2ba8b461` and mine, `17178e75` (found building `#21680`, which kept its 220 px task column on phones because of it).

Repro on `dev` `4b444e4e7a`: open `examples/gantt/basic` at 1440 × 900, then in the App Worker

```js
gantt.taskColumns = [{type: 'tree', dataField: 'title', text: 'Task', width: 160, locked: 'start'}]
```

The page then reports:

```
pageerror: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')
    at src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:419:72
    at Array.map (<anonymous>)
    at Toolbar.passSizeToBody (src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:419:50)
    at Column.syncBodyGeometry (src/timeline/Column.mjs:1129:21)
    at Column.bindGridContext (src/timeline/Column.mjs:538:12)
```

## The Problem

`Neo.gantt.Container#afterSetTaskColumns` rebuilds the columns, and the center header toolbar replaces its `Neo.timeline.TimeAxisHeader`. The new header binds its column while it is still being constructed (`TimeAxisHeader#bindGridContext` → `Column#bindGridContext` → `Column#syncBodyGeometry`), and `syncBodyGeometry` calls `toolbar.passSizeToBody()` because the toolbar is mounted. At that moment the toolbar's one item is still the header's config object. It has no `vdom`, so `items.map(item => item.vdom.id)` throws inside the async method, and the rejection is unhandled.

The measurement it was trying is not needed: the toolbar measures the constructed header right after. A probe wrapping `passSizeToBody` logged the center toolbar's items at each call of one reassignment:

| Call | From | Items |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Column#onConstructed` | the constructed `TimeAxisHeader` |
| 2 | `TimeAxisHeader#bindGridContext` | a plain object, no `vdom`: throws |
| 3 | the toolbar's post-update pass (`Toolbar.mjs:313`) | the constructed `TimeAxisHeader` |

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.grid.header.Toolbar#passSizeToBody` (`src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:395`) measures every item; its dynamic-width branch reads `item.vdom.id` (`:419`).
- The toolbar measures itself once its items have rendered: `promiseUpdate().then(() => mounted && me.passSizeToBody())` (`:313`).
- `Neo.timeline.Column#syncBodyGeometry` (`src/timeline/Column.mjs:1118` on `dev`) calls it whenever the toolbar is mounted, which includes mid-construction.
- `Neo.typeOf(item) === 'NeoInstance'` tells an item from its config (`src/container/Base.mjs:694`).
- Design authority: n/a — an unhandled TypeError is not a behaviour anyone intends.

## The Fix

`Neo.grid.header.Toolbar#passSizeToBody` returns without measuring while any item is not yet an instance: a toolbar between two sets of items has no geometry to report, and its post-update pass reports the new one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reassigning a Gantt's `taskColumns` at runtime reports no error.
- [ ] Afterwards the task column's header and cells take the new width (the guard does not skip the toolbar's real measurement).
- [ ] A Playwright e2e spec proves it: red on `dev` (the `workerErrors` fixture sees the TypeError), green at head.
- [ ] The grid, gantt, scheduler and timeline specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Why the timeline column measures the toolbar while its header is still being constructed.
